districts.reasoning: Rural Middle Shabelle, predominantly AS-controlled, virtually no humanitarian access during much of 2017-2021; nutrition data largely extrapolated, very high uncertainty.
Afgoye corridor hosts one of the largest IDP concentrations near Mogadishu; sustained Serious-Critical GAM; mixed access; relatively strong NGO presence near capital.
Lower Juba mostly rural with AS presence (historical Afmadow exactions); mixed access; agropastoral and livestock-dependent.
Gedo riverine; severely flood-affected 2019 (~55,000 displaced, town partially inundated); North Gedo Riverine had 31.1% GAM in 2020 Deyr; AS rural; mixed access.
Remote southern coastal Lower Juba, very low population density, pastoral; almost no representative survey data through 2017-2021; substantially extrapolated.

Awdal agropastoral district with limited markets. Moderate stress through 2017-21 with poor 2017 Gu/Karan harvest (87% below average). Stable Somaliland governance gives access; no major shocks but modest treatment infrastructure.
Middle Shabelle district close to Mogadishu, mixed government/AS control; flood-exposed; relatively better access than rural ML Shabelle.

Mogadishu - largest IDP-hosting area in Somalia (Mogadishu IDPs Critical GAM 16.7% in 2020 Deyr, sustained Critical since 2016); huge caseload; very strong treatment infrastructure and the most reliable surveillance in country, raising p substantially via both recovery and CFR pathways.
Remote coastal Bari, Coastal Deeh livelihood zone, severe drought 2017 and ongoing pastoral stress 2018-2021. Small samples, poor access.
Coastal Lower Shabelle, official South West State capital but with strong AS presence; remote with mixed access.

Baidoa, epicenter of 2017 famine risk and 2022 Risk of Famine; massive IDP camps with sustained Critical GAM (~16-17%); huge caseload but intensive WFP/UNICEF programs and the AWD/cholera outbreak (half of all 2017 cases in Baidoa town) drive case fatality up. Strong surveillance.

Epicenter of October-November 2019 Shabelle floods (~273,000 displaced, 85% of town inundated); 2020 Deyr flagged Beletweyne urban and IDPs as Critical GAM; 2021 drought; chronic conflict. High caseload but heavy NGO presence.
Gedo border town with mixed control; 2021 drought; partial humanitarian access.
Major port city, urban Somaliland, functional services. Stable food security and lower nutrition stress; some Hargeysa-IDP overflow. Treatment programs operational.

Awdal regional capital, urban Somaliland with functional health system and regular FSNAU surveys. Relatively stable food security throughout 2017-21; treatment programs moderate to good. GAM rates have been Acceptable to Alert.

Large port city and major IDP hub in Puntland. Bossaso IDPs have shown persistent Critical GAM (15.8% in 2020 Deyr; ~21.9% earlier periods); however strong NGO/UNICEF treatment infrastructure raises p. Good surveillance.

Middle Juba is the only Somali region fully and exclusively under AS control. Bu'aale entirely AS, no humanitarian access; chronic SAM endemic; nutrition data essentially absent and extrapolated; case durations very long without treatment.
Hiraan rural, AS-besieged with periodic blockades (Wajid/Bulo-Burte/Hudur cited by HRW); persistent Critical GAM zone; severely restricted humanitarian access.
Major urban Somaliland centre with strong health/nutrition surveillance and treatment programs. IDP settlements moderate. Good regular FSNAU surveys.
Inland Nugaal, NIP livelihood, severe 2017 drought with persistent livestock stress. Moderate access from Garowe.
Contested district on Togdheer/Sool/Cayn boundary, recurrent inter-clan tensions and mixed governance. Northern Inland Pastoral stress; remote with irregular nutrition data.

Bay rural agropastoral - the Bay-Bakool Low Potential Agropastoral livelihood zone classified Emergency (IPC4) in 2017 and again at risk in 2021-2022; AS-influenced rural areas with severely restricted access. Very high incidence, sparse data.
Galgaduud Hawd Pastoral, similar profile to Cadaado; 2021 drought-displaced populations atypical.
Galgaduud Hawd Pastoral, drought 2017 and severe drought 2021 with locust 2020. Moderate access.
Coastal Middle Shabelle, AS influence, agropastoral; flood and conflict exposure. Limited access.
Extreme tip of Horn of Africa, very remote coastal pastoral. Almost no representative survey data; data substantially extrapolated. Persistent NE pastoral stress with very high data uncertainty.
Sool district in Northern Inland Pastoral livelihood zone, extreme drought 2017 with Critical GAM; chronic livestock loss without rapid recovery. Limited treatment infrastructure.
Sanaag East Golis Pastoral, severely affected by 2016-17 drought with persistent pastoral stress. Limited rural treatment programs.
Southern Inland Pastoral of Elberde recorded the highest GAM in 2020 Deyr at 20.9% (Critical IPC4); severe and persistent crisis. AS-influenced rural with limited access.
Galgaduud rural with strong AS presence; 2020 locust epicentre; 2021 drought; very limited humanitarian access reduces both incidence detection and exits.
Galgaduud rural with AS presence; 2020 locust impact; 2021 drought. Limited access, small surveys.
Gedo border with Kenya; AS influence in El Wak rural; 2019 Kenya border closure disrupted markets; limited rural access.
Sanaag regional capital, hit hard by 2017 northern drought (East Golis Pastoral); GAM was Critical (15-30%) in post-Jilaal 2017. Mixed treatment access; recovery 2018-19 then renewed pastoral stress.
Galgaduud capital and IDP-hosting urban centre. Classified Crisis (IPC3) in early 2021; 2022 Risk of Famine flagged for Dhusamareb IDPs. Moderate treatment via NGOs.
Bay agropastoral, AS-influenced; persistent Sorghum-belt failure 2017 and 2021. Very limited rural humanitarian access.
Major IDP hub on Ethiopian border; Dolow IDPs Critical GAM persistent (~26.4% in 2015, sustained since); strong NGO presence including LWF, GREDO; good surveillance and treatment.
Coastal Nugaal, Coastal Deeh / NIP livelihood, severe 2017 drought, partial water-source recovery only. Remote, small samples.
Split city (Puntland north / Galmudug south), one of the largest IDP hubs. Galkacyo IDPs persistently Critical GAM (~21.8%); 2022 Risk of Famine flagged. Strong programs but persistent caseload.
North Mudug, Hawd Pastoral, drought-affected 2017 and 2021. Moderate access from Gaalkacyo.
Gedo regional capital, mixed access; 2017 drought-related distress migration to Doolow/Banadir; 2021 drought severe. Moderate treatment infrastructure.
Puntland capital and major IDP centre. Garowe IDPs persistently Critical GAM (15.8% in 2020 Deyr, 17.6% in 2017 Deyr); strong treatment programs and good surveillance lift p above national norm.
Stable Somaliland agropastoral district near Hargeysa with good road access and treatment availability. Low chronic stress.

Largest urban centre in Somaliland with the strongest health and nutrition system, strong NGO presence, and high-quality regular surveillance. IDP populations show Serious GAM but treatment coverage is high, accelerating exits.
South Mudug coastal, partially Al-Shabaab influenced (Harardhere/Hobyo coastal swathes). Drought, locust 2020, remote. Limited treatment access.
Remote eastern Bari, very low population density, pastoral livelihood, severe NE drought 2017. Sparse, irregular surveys.
Hiraan rural Shabelle riverine, mostly AS-controlled, flood-affected 2019; specifically named in 2018 Post-Gu as area of concern. Very limited treatment access.
Lower Juba riverine, 2019 flood-affected and 2020 Deyr Juba Riverine flagged Critical GAM; AS-influenced rural; limited access.
Coastal/Addun pastoral Mudug, severe drought 2017 with only partial water-source recovery. Remote, irregular surveys.
Middle Juba, key AS economic hub, fully AS-controlled; riverine; no humanitarian access; chronic endemic SAM with effectively no treatment exits.

Middle Shabelle capital, severe 2019 flooding (10,000+ ha cropland damaged in Jowhar/Mahaday Weyne); riverine livelihood zones in 2020 Deyr classified Critical GAM (15.4%). Mixed access, regional capital.
Lower Juba regional capital, IJA-controlled with major IDP populations (Dhobley/Kismayo IDPs); 2021 drought severe; functional treatment programs and decent surveillance.
Remote Lower Shabelle, AS-controlled with very poor access; nutrition data largely extrapolated.
Sool regional centre and contested capital, NIP severe drought 2017 caused Critical GAM; moderate urban services; FSNAU surveys regular.
Coastal Sanaag, contested between Somaliland and Puntland claims; remote with very poor road access and small/irregular surveys.

Coastal Awdal in Guban Pastoral livelihood zone, classified Emergency (IPC4) in 2018 Deyr from 4-6 consecutive failed seasons. Remote, small population, limited surveys. Persistent pastoral stress drives steady incidence.
Gedo border riverine town, 2019 flood-affected, 2021 severe drought; moderate access; some NGO presence.
Lower Shabelle regional capital, mixed AS/government control; 2019 flash floods damaged 200+ ha; chronic IDP burden. Mixed humanitarian access, conflict-driven displacement.
Togdheer agropastoral, deteriorated to Crisis (IPC3) in late 2018 / early 2019 from poor Deyr. Limited treatment outside larger settlements. Moderate data variability.
Remote coastal Bari, similar profile to Bandarbeyla; poor access, small irregular surveys.
Bay rural agropastoral, AS-influenced; same crisis profile as Diinsoor. Limited access.
Major Puntland urban centre, Qardho IDPs persistently Critical GAM through 2017-2018 (~21.9%); functional treatment though smaller than Bossaso. Regular surveys.
Lower Shabelle riverine, AS-influenced; 2020 Q1 clashes between AS and clan militias caused asset losses; persistent crisis. Limited access.
Remote Bakool, AS-controlled, very limited access; data largely extrapolated.
Middle Juba, fully AS-controlled, riverine; no humanitarian access through 2017-2021; data largely extrapolated.
Remote Lower Shabelle, AS-controlled; data largely extrapolated. Persistent agropastoral stress.
Small mountainous district in Sahil/Togdheer, relatively low population. Generally stable but small samples cause moderate variability in survey results.
Remote Sool district with very poor road access (rendered impassable in 2019 floods); contested governance and small/irregular nutrition surveys cause high data variability.
Bakool rural, predominantly AS-controlled with very poor humanitarian access; nutrition data sparse and uncertain.
Bakool, AS-besieged historically (cited alongside Hudur and Bulo-Burte); 2014 cereal prices quadrupled; persistent crisis profile through 2017-2021.
Lower Shabelle rural, AS heavy presence; 2021 clashes; agropastoral stress. Limited humanitarian access.
South Mudug coastal under historic AS influence; 2020 desert locust impact; chronic pastoral stress. Limited access.
Among the most remote contested Sool districts; FAO/SWALIM 2019 study explicitly noted Xudun was 'largely inaccessible' due to roads. Sparse data, persistent pastoral stress.

Hudur, Bakool capital, AS-besieged with periodic blockades; Hudur urban/IDPs Critical GAM 16.4% in 2020 Deyr; classified Crisis (IPC3). Some humanitarian access in town but severe rural inaccessibility.
Far-northwest border district in Guban Pastoral, severely drought-affected 2017-2018. Very remote, sparse data quality, limited treatment access despite Somaliland governance.
